title: add_observation

item_id.description: Only for a callback without an incoming source: the stored document that establishes this observation, ITM-… for a collected item or web-… for a page read with fetch_page; find it with read-only SQL (tank-data data guide, «Finding record IDs for tool arguments»), «Source document by URL». Omit when an incoming source is supplied.

type.description: Atomic claim kind. Use STATE when the verbatim quote establishes an event or integration stage and set state_claim explicitly. FACT describes a fact but FACT with state_claim null does not advance the event stage. NUMBER, RELATION, TIMESTAMP, MECHANISM and MILESTONE retain their evidence contracts.

subject.description: Short plain-language subject, e.g. 'OJK'. Printed on the card.

predicate.description: Plain-language verb phrase as it reads in a sentence, e.g. 'expects trading to start on', never snake_case. Printed on the card.

object.description: Short plain-language object, at most about 12 words; details stay in the quote. Printed on the card.

state_claim.description: Agent-assigned stage asserted by this claim. Use STATE for a stage assertion and the highest quote-supported stage; null is valid for unknown or non-stage claims. A proposal/request is PROPOSED; an official committed future plan is APPROVED, not deployment or live operation. One-sided compatibility, SDK or repository evidence supports at most BUILT on the integration ladder and never limits event state. Supply verified separately; Tank records both without semantic rechecking.

quote.description: Verbatim atomic quote. Omit evidence when it comes from the incoming source; otherwise cite the stored document containing it in evidence (a page read with fetch_page is its own document, even when its URL matches the discovery item).

token_ids.description: Registry token keys (reg.tokens), shown after « · » next to the name in Tank's messages and results, e.g. bitcoin:BTC or uniswap:UNI.

claim_ids.description: Claim IDs (CLM-…) of accepted claims of the current event; find them with read-only SQL (tank-data data guide, «Finding record IDs for tool arguments»), «Claims of an event».

approval_dependency.description: Explicit thesis dependency of a REJECTED approval: the accepted causal RELATION claims of the current event it rests on (claim_ids) and, for TOKEN scope, the registry tokens it concerns (token_ids). Tank validates the IDs and their scope; it does not infer dependencies from text.

verified.description: Agent-assigned verification under claim rule V2: true only for HIGH-certainty support; LIVE or higher also needs explicit availability or a market/technical artifact. Tank stores this flag without semantic rechecking.

verification_missing.description: Agent-supplied explanation of what confirmation is missing for this unverified claim (for example, no announcement from the named organization). Tank preserves and displays it verbatim; null means the reason was not established. Keep it to about 10 words; it is printed in NOT VERIFIED.

supersedes_claim_ids.description: Claim IDs (CLM-…) of prior claims of the current event that this claim replaces on the current card; the old claims remain historical evidence. Omit unrelated claims and remaining uncertainties; find them with read-only SQL (tank-data data guide, «Finding record IDs for tool arguments»), «Claims of an event».

evidence.description: The stored document containing this claim's quote, by item_id. Omit for a quote from the incoming source. For text read with fetch_page or web_search, cite that stored document, not the discovery document merely because its URL matches. The observation's own document is the incoming source, or the item_id given for a callback without one.

item_id.description: ID of a stored source document: ITM-… for a collected item, web-… for a page read with fetch_page or a web_search result; find it with read-only SQL (tank-data data guide, «Finding record IDs for tool arguments»), «Source document by URL».

certainty.description: Optional agent-supplied certainty update when reassessed: HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW. Tank stores it as supplied; omission preserves the existing event certainty without implicit promotion.

certainty_reason.description: Optional reason when certainty is reassessed. Tank stores it as supplied; omission preserves the existing reason without inferring a new judgment.

timing_confidence.description: Agent-supplied confidence in the event timing: HIGH for an exact primary timestamp, MEDIUM for bucket precision, LOW for collection time only. Optional; omission leaves declared timestamp precision as the timing-confidence basis.

description: Add claims to the current event. The host binds the incoming source; for a callback without one (MILESTONE, CONDITION_FIRED, CALL_EXPIRED, USER_QUESTION), pass the item_id of the stored document that establishes the update, such as a page read with fetch_page. Cite claim evidence by item_id and replace prior claims of this event with supersedes_claim_ids.
